**Key Design Elements of an IT/OT‑Based Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS)** | Layer / Element | What it is | Why it matters for an IT/OT‑converged ADMS | |-----------------|------------|-------------------------------------------| | **Field‑Level OT (Operation Technology)** | • Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs), smart meters, sensors, switches, reclosers, DER inverters, RTUs.
• Real‑time measurements (voltage, current, power quality, status). | Provides the “physical” data that the ADMS must ingest and act on. | | **Communication & Protocol Stack** | • IEC 61850‑MMS, DNP3, IEC 60870‑5‑104, Modbus‑TCP, MQTT, OPC‑UA.
• Secure, low‑latency, redundant fiber / wireless / PLC networks. | Guarantees deterministic, interoperable data exchange between OT devices and IT services. | | **Middleware / Integration Platform (IT‑OT Bridge)** | • Data‑aggregation servers, historians, message brokers, API gateways.
• Common data model (CIM/IEC 61970‑61982) and semantic adapters. | “Blurs” the IT/OT boundary – normalises heterogeneous OT streams into IT‑friendly formats for analytics and applications. | | **Core IT Services** | • SCADA/EMS, Distribution Automation System (DAS), GIS, Asset Management, Cyber‑Security services.
• Cloud/edge compute nodes, containerised micro‑services. | Supplies the traditional supervisory, planning and optimisation functions that ADMS builds upon. | | **Advanced Analytics & Decision‑Support** | • Load forecasting, fault location‑isolation‑restoration (FLISR), Volt‑VAR optimisation (VVO), DER coordination, outage prediction.
• Machine‑learning models, state‑estimation, optimisation engines. | Turns raw OT data into actionable insights; the “advanced” part of ADMS. | | **Human‑Machine Interface (HMI) / Visualization** | • Real‑time dashboards, GIS‑based maps, alarm panels, mobile apps.
• Role‑based access, drill‑down to device level. | Enables operators to monitor, diagnose and intervene quickly. | | **Control & Actuation Layer** | • Automated set‑point changes, switch operations, DER dispatch, demand‑response commands.
• Closed‑loop control loops with latency guarantees. | Closes the feedback loop – the ADMS not only sees the network, it actively steers it. | | **Security & Governance** | • Identity & access management, PKI, network segmentation, intrusion detection, patch management.
• Compliance with NERC‑CIP, IEC 62443, ISO 27001. | Protects the converged IT/OT environment from cyber‑threats while preserving reliability. | | **Scalability & Resilience Architecture** | • Horizontal scaling (micro‑services, container orchestration), edge‑cloud hierarchy, high‑availability clusters.
• Redundant data paths, graceful degradation. | Guarantees that the ADMS can grow with the distribution network and survive failures. | --- **Core Convergence Concepts that Bind the Design Together** | Concept | Description | Practical Implication for ADMS | |---------|-------------|--------------------------------| | **Interoperability** | Use of open, standards‑based protocols and data models (IEC 61850, CIM, OPC‑UA) so that OT devices can speak directly to IT applications. | Reduces vendor lock‑in, simplifies integration of new sensors, DERs, and legacy equipment. | | **Unified Data Model** | Mapping of OT telemetry into a common information model (CIM) that IT services can query uniformly. | Enables a single source of truth for analytics, reduces data silos, and speeds up application development. | | **IT‑OT Boundary Blurring** | Physical devices (OT) are no longer isolated “black boxes”; they expose APIs and telemetry that IT systems can consume in real time. | Allows the ADMS to run advanced algorithms (e.g., ML) on live field data and to push control actions back instantly. | | **Edge‑to‑Cloud Continuum** | Critical, latency‑sensitive functions (e.g., protection, local VVO) run at the edge; heavy‑weight analytics and long‑term storage reside in the cloud/central data centre. | Balances performance (fast local response) with scalability (centralised analytics). | | **Cyber‑Physical Security Integration** | Security controls are embedded in both IT and OT layers (network segmentation, device hardening, continuous monitoring). | Prevents the “weakest link” problem where a compromised OT device could jeopardise the whole ADMS. | | **Service‑Oriented Architecture (SOA) / Micro‑services** | ADMS functions (forecasting, FLISR, VVO, DER coordination) are packaged as independent services with well‑defined APIs. | Facilitates rapid deployment of new features, easier testing, and independent scaling of each function. | | **Real‑Time Data Fusion** | Continuous ingestion of high‑frequency SCADA/PMU data together with slower asset‑management or weather feeds. | Provides a holistic, up‑to‑the‑second view of the distribution network for optimal decision‑making. | | **Lifecycle‑Centric Design** | The system is built to support not only operation but also planning, maintenance, and de‑commissioning phases. | Enables seamless transition from design‑time studies to real‑time control, and back to asset‑management. | | **Governance & Standards Alignment** | Alignment with industry standards (NERC‑CIP, IEC 62443, IEEE 1547 for DERs) and internal utility policies. | Ensures regulatory compliance and smooth integration with existing utility processes. | --- ### How to “Distill” the Design into a Practical Blueprint 1. **Define the Architecture Layers** – Map OT devices → Communication → Middleware (IT‑OT bridge) → Core IT services → Advanced analytics → HMI/Control. 2. **Select Standards Early** – Adopt IEC 61850 for substation/field communication, CIM for data modelling, and OPC‑UA for cross‑domain APIs. 3. **Build an Integration Platform** – Deploy a message broker (e.g., MQTT or Kafka) and a historian that normalise all incoming telemetry into the CIM model. 4. **Implement Security by Design** – Apply network segmentation (OT VLANs, DMZ), PKI‑based device authentication, and continuous monitoring dashboards. 5. **Deploy Edge Compute for Time‑Critical Functions** – Run FLISR, local VVO, and protection logic on edge gateways; push aggregated results to the central ADMS. 6. **Develop Micro‑service‑Based ADMS Functions** – Package each advanced function (load forecast, DER dispatch, outage prediction) as a containerised service with REST/GraphQL APIs. 7. **Provide a Unified HMI** – Build a GIS‑centric dashboard that can drill from system‑wide view down to individual IED status, with role‑based access. 8. **Plan for Scalability & Resilience** – Use container orchestration (Kubernetes) for auto‑scaling, and design redundant data paths (dual‑homed fiber, backup LTE). 9. **Establish Governance Processes** – Define data‑ownership, change‑management, and compliance checks that span both IT and OT teams. 10. **Iterate with Pilot Projects** – Start with a limited feeder, validate end‑to‑end data flow, security, and control actions, then roll out to the wider network. --- **Bottom‑Line Summary** - **Key design elements** are the layered architecture (field OT → communication → IT‑OT bridge → core IT services → analytics → HMI/control) together with standards‑based protocols, a unified data model, edge‑cloud distribution, micro‑service implementation, and built‑in cyber‑security. - **Convergence concepts** are interoperability, blurring of the IT/OT boundary, real‑time data fusion, service‑oriented design, and a security‑by‑design mindset that treats the distribution network as a cyber‑physical system. By embedding these elements and concepts into the system blueprint, an ADMS can truly leverage the strengths of both IT (big‑data analytics, cloud scalability, flexible software) and OT (real‑time device control, reliability) to deliver higher reliability, better integration of distributed energy resources, and more efficient distribution‑grid operation.

hits.title: IT/OT Convergence 기반의 Advanced Distribution Management System의 설계
hits.abstract: Power automation system to operate power distribution systems can be distinguished by distribution SCADA with remote monitoring and control; and distribution automation system with basic functions such as service restoration to the distribution SCADA; and distribution management system which is operated by various applications in order to enhance distribution system operation performance based on the distribution automation system. In the technological change, a technical boundary of information technology (IT) and operation technology (OT) is being blurred by that new concepts such as interoperability. In addtion, IT/OT convergence has been proposed by the improvement of ICT and power system technology. At the viewpoint, advanced distribution management system (ADMS) to have the new concepts and to increase distribution system operation efficiency through global information and functions from the other systems has been proposed. In order to implement the ADMS, IT and OT have to be employed together on the ADMS; and the concept-based IT/OT convergence concept has been presented. Therefore, this paper introduces ADMS and IT/OT convergence and proposes a design of IT/OT convergence based ADMS system design with configurations and functions.
